posts.title: How to get your brand cited by ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity
posts.excerpt: AI assistants are the new front page. Here is the practical checklist we use to make brands easy for them to understand, trust and quote.
posts.author: Spotlight Team
posts.body:
When someone asks an AI assistant *"which agency should I hire"* or *"what's the best moisturiser for dry skin"*, the answer it gives is the new front page of the internet. If your brand isn't in that answer, you are invisible to a growing share of buyers.

The good news: the work that gets you cited is concrete. Here is the checklist we run for every client.

## 1. Say what you are, in one plain sentence

AI models summarise. Make the summary easy. Your homepage, About page and social bios should all contain the same clear line: who you are, what you do, and for whom. Consistency across the web is a trust signal.

## 2. Answer real questions on your own pages

List the 20 questions customers ask before buying, then answer each one in two or three direct sentences. Put the best ones in an FAQ with FAQPage structured data. Question-led content is exactly what answer engines look for.

## 3. Add structured data everywhere it fits

- Organization and LocalBusiness or ProfessionalService
- Product, Offer and Review where they are real
- Article, FAQPage, Event and VideoObject

Structured data turns your pages from text into facts a machine can use.

## 4. Publish an llms.txt file

A short Markdown file at `/llms.txt` that tells AI crawlers what your site is about and where the important pages live. It takes ten minutes and costs nothing.

## 5. Let the right crawlers in

Check your robots.txt. Many sites block AI crawlers by accident. Decide deliberately which ones you allow.

## 6. Earn mentions, not just links

Assistants learn from what others say about you: reviews, press, directories, community threads. A steady drumbeat of genuine mentions matters more than one big backlink.

> The brands that win AI search are the ones that are easiest to describe accurately.

Want to know how visible you are today? Our free growth audit includes an AI-visibility check.

faq.a: GEO is the practice of making your brand easy for AI assistants to understand, trust and cite, using clear facts, structured data, question-led content and consistent mentions across the web.
Yes. AI assistants lean heavily on pages that already rank and load fast. GEO builds on good SEO rather than replacing it.

posts.title: Stop guessing your Meta ads: a simple creative testing system
posts.excerpt: Most ad accounts don't have a targeting problem, they have a creative problem. A lightweight testing rhythm that small teams can actually run.
posts.author: Spotlight Team
posts.body:
Meta's delivery system is very good at finding people. What it can't do is fix an ad nobody wants to watch. That is why creative is now the biggest lever in most accounts.

## Test ideas, not button colours

A useful test changes the **idea**: the hook, the promise, the format. Swapping one word in a headline rarely teaches you anything.

## A weekly rhythm

1. Monday: launch three to five new concepts in a dedicated testing campaign.
2. Thursday: read early signals: hook rate, hold rate, click-through, cost per result.
3. Next Monday: move the winner into your scaling campaign and retire the losers.

## Track the right numbers

- **Hook rate**: the share of impressions that watch the first three seconds
- **Hold rate**: how many keep watching to the end
- **Cost per result**: the number that pays the bills

## Feed the machine good data

Set up the Meta Pixel *and* the Conversions API, deduplicated with a shared event ID, so the algorithm sees every lead and sale even when browsers block cookies.

Get these basics right and every rupee you spend teaches you something.

faq.q: How many creatives should I test at once?
faq.a: For most small and mid-size budgets, three to five new concepts a week is enough to learn quickly without spreading spend too thin.

posts.title: The 20-point checklist we run before any website goes live
posts.excerpt: Privacy policy to page speed, spam protection to social previews. The unglamorous details that decide whether a beautiful site actually works.
posts.author: Spotlight Team
posts.body:
A website can look stunning and still leak leads. Before we launch anything, we tick every box below.

## Trust and legal

- Privacy policy and terms and conditions
- Cookie consent banner that blocks tracking until the visitor agrees
- HTTPS enforced everywhere
- No secret keys in front-end code

## Findability

- Unique meta titles and descriptions on every page
- Social preview image for WhatsApp, LinkedIn and X
- Favicon in every size
- sitemap.xml and robots.txt
- Descriptive alt text on images

## Speed and access

- Compressed images and video
- A page speed check on mobile
- Colour contrast that passes WCAG AA
- Fully responsive on phones

## Reliability

- A custom 404 page
- No broken links
- Form validation with clear error messages
- Spam protection on every form
- Analytics set up and tested

## Focus

- **One** clear call to action

That last one matters most. Every page should make the next step obvious.
